claims.text: Thermal Gradient Annealing with Staged Cooling induces controlled atomic ordering in non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
The induced atomic ordering shifts magnetic transition temperatures.
The treatment enhances the magnetocaloric effect relative to conventional processing.
Rapidly solidified or as-cast non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys have homogeneous but unoptimized atomic arrangements.
A treatment consisting of approximately 900°C for 30 seconds, 700°C for 60 seconds, and 500°C for 60 seconds followed by quenching can tune the alloy.
Rapid temperature changes and precise holding times allow the alloy to traverse different free-energy minima.
Staged thermal treatment alters atomic-ordering motifs and causes microstructural rearrangements.
Altered atomic ordering and microstructure modify the balance of magnetic exchange interactions.
Sampling multiple free-energy minima produces microstructural states with tuned magnetic exchange couplings.
Tuned magnetic exchange couplings shift magnetic ordering temperatures.
Tuned magnetic exchange couplings enhance the magnetocaloric effect.
Staged cooling will produce a measurable shift in Curie or Néel temperature relative to direct quenching or standard isothermal annealing.
Staged cooling will increase the magnetocaloric response, such as the isothermal entropy-change magnitude, relative to conventional processing.
The proposed effect occurs only under low-dimensional processing conditions.
The effect may not occur under single-temperature equilibrium processing or traditional processing.
